questions.note: Height and head size match the drawing and the legs follow the declared real thighs. But the shoulder line is wider and squarer than the reference's (about 8 % across the pauldrons), the upper arms are puffed out, and the neck reads thick. He looks heavier in the upper body and less lean V-taper than the drawn man.

Stance, foot spacing, head turn and the carbine's diagonal all follow the onion closely. The silhouette breaks at the right shoulder, where a raised pauldron slab sticks up past the drawn outline, at the forearms (slimmer guards), and at the ankles, where bloused cuffs and tall boot shafts replace trousers falling over mid-cut boots.

Every item is roughly where the drawing puts it: gaiter, carrier, antenna, hip and thigh rigs, knee pads, boots. Several are the wrong size or form: the right pauldron is too big and too high, both forearm guards are short bands, the front pouches are short and open-topped, and the boots are tall-shafted. The emblem is wrong.

The stack order is right and I see no garment passing through another at these views. The carrier sits on the shirt, the belt and thigh straps wrap the trousers, and the gaiter sits under the straps. Against that, the right pauldron stands off the deltoid, the left hand does not close on the handguard, and the trousers are bloused above the boots instead of falling over them.

The kit is lighter than drawn. The carrier is thinner, with narrow shoulder straps and small pouches. The forearm guards are thin bands, not the bulky segmented gauntlets, and the gloves are thin and smooth. Meanwhile the sleeves and upper arms are inflated and the lower trouser legs balloon, so the bulk sits in the wrong places.

The stock tucks under the right arm and the right hand holds the grip with the index finger laid along the receiver, as drawn. The left hand is wrong: it lies over the top of the handguard with nearly straight fingers draped down the near side. The reference wraps it under the handguard with curled fingers, and in the three-quarter-left view it reads open-palmed.

defects.what: The right pauldron is an oversized flat slab tilted up and out. It stands above and outboard of the shoulder line, where the reference has a smaller curved shell with articulated plates seated on the deltoid.
defects.fix: A domed shell about the size of the deltoid with a second articulated plate below, strapped flush to the upper arm; its top no higher than the carrier strap.

defects.what: The left pauldron is two flat cards. The reference has a domed shoulder shell with a raised emblem panel, and below it a segmented plate carrying a small box.
defects.fix: A curved cap that follows the deltoid, with a raised inset panel for the emblem, and a separate lower plate with the side box.

defects.what: The emblem is a pale star-like mark. The reference shows a dark steel-blue inset panel with a light crossed-X device, so the identity mark is wrong.
defects.fix: Reproduce the drawn device: a dark blue-grey panel with the light crossed-X mark, set into the pauldron shell.

defects.what: The right forearm guard is a short double band at mid-forearm and the elbow is bare sleeve. The reference has a long segmented gauntlet from elbow to glove cuff, over a padded elbow.
defects.fix: Make the guard run from just below the elbow to the glove cuff in overlapping segments, with an elbow cap, as drawn.

defects.what: The left forearm guard sits about 60 px high and is short, leaving bare sleeve between it and the glove. The reference guard covers the forearm down to the glove cuff.
defects.fix: Lengthen the guard and move it down so it overlaps the glove cuff, leaving no sleeve exposed at the wrist.

defects.what: The left hand rests over the top of the handguard with nearly straight fingers draped down the near side, not gripping. The reference wraps the hand under the handguard with the fingers curled around it.
defects.fix: A support-hand grip from below: palm under the handguard, fingers curled up around the far side, thumb over the top, all in contact.

defects.what: The gloves are thin and smooth, with long sausage-like fingers and no knuckle armour, finger pads or cuff. The reference gloves are bulky impact gloves with moulded knuckle guards.
defects.fix: Mechanix M-Pact class: a raised moulded knuckle bar, padded finger segments, a thicker palm and a velcro cuff.

defects.what: The front holds three short open-topped pouches. The reference carries taller flapped magazine and admin pouches that hang well below the plate bag, and broad padded shoulder straps with ladder webbing.
defects.fix: Taller flapped pouches reaching about the navel, a central admin pouch, and wide padded shoulder straps with webbing loops.

defects.what: The carrier's Cordura is a flat grey-olive with almost no wear. The reference carrier is a warmer coyote-olive, heavily scuffed, with pale edge wear and grime.
defects.fix: Shift the hue toward olive-coyote, raise saturation a little, and add edge abrasion and grime to the plate bag, straps and pouches.

defects.what: The pauldrons and forearm guards read pale beige-grey with a soft camo mottle. The reference plates are darker blue-grey steel tones, worn, with tan edge chipping.
defects.fix: Darken the plates to a desaturated blue-grey, with localised wear on the edges and corners instead of an all-over mottle.

defects.what: The knee pads are flat rounded-rectangle slabs with pale mottled faces. The reference caps are dark charcoal, with a raised faceted hexagonal centre plate inside a tan rim and a lower lobe over the shin.
defects.fix: A cap with a raised faceted inner plate, a dark face and a tan rim, its lower edge tapering over the top of the shin.

defects.what: The boots have tall shafts and a smooth, slick, rubber-like upper with a low, pointed toe. The reference boots are mid-cut, scuffed leather and suede, with a rounded bulbous toe cap and a chunky lugged sole.
defects.fix: A mid-cut Zephyr-class boot: matte scuffed leather and suede panels, a rounded toe cap, and the shaft hidden under the trouser hem.

defects.what: The trouser legs are bloused tight in a bunched cuff above an exposed boot shaft. In the reference the trouser legs fall loose over the boot collars.
defects.fix: Let the hem drop over the boot collar, with a soft break at the front and no elastic cuff.

defects.what: The shoulders and upper arms are broader and squarer than drawn, and the sleeves are inflated, so the upper body reads bulkier than the reference's lean V-taper.
defects.fix: Narrow the shoulder span to the drawn width and slim the sleeve volume to a fitted combat shirt over the arm.

defects.what: The hair is a solid cap shell with a hard, straight, high hairline and spikes poking out on top. The reference has short textured hair, longer and swept up on top, with faded sides and a natural hairline.
defects.fix: Strand or card hair: faded sides, about 3 to 5 cm on top swept up and back, and a hairline that dips lower at the temples with a soft edge.

defects.what: The gaiter is a smooth cone whose top sits low, exposing neck. The reference gaiter bunches in thick folds right up under the jaw.
defects.fix: A thicker, looser tube with stacked folds, its top edge at the jawline.

defects.what: The trousers carry hard-edged pale camo blotches. The reference trousers are dark charcoal with diffuse dust and grime, heavier on the thighs and shins.
defects.fix: A darker base with soft, wear-driven dust gradients instead of printed blotches.

ranked: [D1] The right pauldron is a raised flat slab sticking up past the shoulder; it is the first thing that breaks the drawn outline. The real thing is a curved shell seated on the deltoid.
[D14] The upper body is too broad and puffy: square shoulders and inflated sleeves make him heavier than the lean, tapered man in the reference.
[D4] [D5] Both forearm guards are short bands. The drawn bulky segmented gauntlets reaching the gloves are a signature of the silhouette, and their absence changes the arms.
[D10] The plates (pauldrons, guards, knee pads) are pale beige-grey camo mottle instead of dark blue-grey worn steel tones with tan edge chipping, so the armour reads like plastic.
[D6] The left hand lies over the handguard instead of wrapping under it, so the hold no longer reads as the reference's ready grip.
[D15] The hair is a cap shell with a straight, high hairline and spikes. Identity suffers even with the declared parametric face.
[D12] The boots are tall, slick and rubber-like with pointed toes; the reference has mid-cut, scuffed, round-toed leather boots.
[D13] The bloused cuffs over exposed boot shafts change the ankles; the reference's trousers fall over the boots.
[D8] The carrier front is underbuilt: short open pouches and narrow straps where the reference has tall flapped pouches and broad padded straps.
[D9] The carrier is a flat grey-olive with almost no wear, against the reference's warm, scuffed coyote-olive.
[D11] The knee pads are flat slabs with pale faces, missing the faceted hex centre plate and the dark face inside the tan rim.
[D7] The gloves are thin and smooth with sausage fingers; the reference wears bulky knuckle-armoured impact gloves.
[D3] The emblem is a pale star; the reference shows a dark panel with a crossed-X device.
[D2] The left pauldron is flat cards, not a domed shell with a raised emblem panel.
[D16] The gaiter is a smooth cone sitting low on the neck; the reference bunches up under the jaw.
[D17] The trousers have hard-edged printed blotches where the reference shows diffuse dust and grime on a charcoal base.
Overall the render is cleaner and lower in contrast than the reference: wear is spread evenly rather than concentrated on edges and contact points.
